answer: Each lotus must present an attestation quote from its own secure enclave and burn onyx to register it in the nebula, a registry of enclave keys and the networks hosting them. A reused key collides there and is rejected outright, and the k-th lotus whose enclave sits in an already-registered network burns k² onyx. An honest lotus burns 1 onyx, but 1,000 clones in one rented datacenter burn about 333 million onyx, the last alone 1 million. It breaks if enclave keys can be extracted or forged, or if hosts can be spread across many networks cheaply.
